classification.difficultyReason: The decisive unsignposted step is to fix one element and toggle its membership, pairing even and odd subsets. The student must recognise that this operation reverses itself and therefore proves a bijection.

content.prompt: Let $X$ be a non-empty set with finite cardinality. Prove that the number of subsets of $X$ with even cardinality is equal to the number of subsets of $X$ with odd cardinality.

answer.short:
The two numbers are equal.

Fix an element of $X$. Adding or removing this element pairs every even-cardinality subset with exactly one odd-cardinality subset.
answer.worked:
Choose $x_0\in X$. Let $E$ and $O$ be the families of subsets of $X$ with even and odd cardinality, respectively. Define $f:E\to O$ by
$$f(S)=\begin{cases}S\cup\{x_0\},&x_0\notin S,\\S\setminus\{x_0\},&x_0\in S.\end{cases}$$
Adding or removing one element changes the parity of the cardinality, so $f(S)\in O$. Applying the same operation again returns $S$. Thus distinct even-cardinality subsets have distinct images, and every odd-cardinality subset has an even-cardinality preimage. Therefore $f$ is bijective, and $|E|=|O|$.
